context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Stop returning every user record to any caller. Require authentication on this route for all HTTP methods, and derive ownership from the authenticated session or token, never from a path or body identifier. Replace the unscoped `UserModel.findAll()` with a query limited to the authenticated Data Principal's own record, e.g. `UserModel.findAll({ where: { id: req.user.id } })` (or `findOne` for a single record). Only return a broader set when the authenticated user holds an explicit role authorised for that data, checked server-side on every request, such as `if (req.user.role !== 'admin') return 403`. Apply the same middleware and ownership or role check to every other method on the route (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and so on), so the controls cover all access to the Personal Data as Rule 6(1)(b) requires. Return only the minimum fields needed, and add tests that confirm unauthenticated requests get 401, a user cannot read another user's record by changing an ID, and an unauthorised role gets 403.
